results.reasoning: Censorship is a means of preventing (A). Protect from heresy (B). Rigid (C) system in Sparta.
Universally (A) throughout history. Impiety (B) = asebeia. Eliminate (C) opponents.
Ideological (A) error alongside heresy/treason. Divine (B) anger from gods. Identical (C) with repression.
③locally is wrong; original says universally throughout Greek history.
②celebrated is wrong; Sparta banned books/music/learned men.
④mild is wrong; original says harsh repression.
Sparta's rigid censorship protected its militarism. Banning books/music confirms military culture.
The common charge was impiety, confirmed by parenthetical (asebeia).
Silence and eliminate opponents - logical target of tyrannical censorship.
banned = prohibited (both mean forbidden).
imposed = enforced (both mean compelled/forced into effect).
eliminate = remove (both mean get rid of).
rigid ↔ flexible (stiff vs bendable/adaptable).
repression ↔ liberation (suppression vs freedom).
(A) charge = accusation in legal context. (B) charge = fee in commerce context.
Official suppression of objectionable material = censorship by definition.
Noun ideology → adjective ideological to modify error.
Noun impiety → adjective impious to modify behaviour.
Authorities practise censorship 'in the name of the common good' - seeking to protect from heresy/treason.
Under tyrants, censorship was identical with harsh repression - final sentence conclusion.
